patent: Published application US 2022/0106338 A1, CBN Nano Technologies, filed 2021-11-22, published 2022-04-07; later granted as US 11,708,384 B2. Proposes atomically precise tips made in bulk by solution chemistry and bonded to a surface, in place of tips built by mechanosynthesis, so a scanning probe can use many pre-loaded tips once each. FIG. 1-17 show the tips; FIG. 18-43, 46 and 50-53 synthetic routes; FIG. 44-45 cap removal; FIG. 47-49 apparatus. Experiments in the document itself: deposition of the FIG. 51-53 molecules on Si(100), with X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy indicating 50% of legs bonded, 86% after one anneal to 200 C, from which the text infers at least 19% of tips with all three legs bonded ([0203]-[0204]). It reports no mechanosynthetic reaction performed with these tips and does not say which of the other routes were run; [0198] cites molecular modeling for bromine passivation.

figs.1: Abstraction tip, modules labelled. Plain adamantane cage, three CH2 legs each ending in S, bonded to a blank surface box. The dot on top of the triple bond marks the unpaired electron [0104]. No feedstock is drawn.
figs.2: Hydrogen donation tip. Against FIG. 1 every module changes: Ge replaces the apex carbon and holds H as feedstock, legs are trifluorophenyl rings, linkers are O.
figs.3: AbstractO. Carbon cage with a C2 radical on top; trifluorophenyl legs; O linkers; Si. Set FIG. 3-7 changes only what sits on top of the cage.
figs.4: HDonationO. Ge at the cage apex holds H.
figs.5: C2DonationO. Same C2 radical as FIG. 3, but on Ge: here it is feedstock [0137]; on carbon in FIG. 3 it is the abstraction site.
figs.6: MeDonationO. Ge holds a CH2 radical.
figs.7: One drawing for four tips: the printed key M = Si, Ge and R = -H, -CH3 gives SiH3, GeH3, SiMe3 or GeMe3 feedstock.
figs.8: AbstractNH ("AbstractionNH" in [0138]). FIG. 3 with each O linker replaced by NH. Set FIG. 8-12 mirrors FIG. 3-7.
figs.12: FIG. 7 with NH linkers; same M and R key.
figs.13: AbstractS ("AbstractionS" in [0139]). The aryl legs are gone: CH2 legs and S linkers on Au. Set FIG. 13-17 mirrors FIG. 3-7. [0136]: Au has weaker intra-surface bonds than Si, which limits pulling forces.
figs.14: HDonationS. Ge-H on the short CH2-S legs.
figs.17: Repeated on the front page. M and R key as FIG. 7. Brief description [0034] says "on Silicon"; the drawing and [0139] show gold.
figs.18: AbstractO route, OFA-1 to OFA-9. Triol plus trifluorophenol builds the three legs; the remaining bridgehead then runs OH, CO2H, ester, CH2OH, CHO, iodoalkyne. Phenols stay TBS-protected from OFA-5 to OFA-8. OFA-9 has free OH for binding and an I cap (removal in FIG. 44).
figs.19: HDonationO route from FHD-104X (FIG. 42). Ge-X to Ge-H (FHD-105), then TBDPS removal gives FHD-106.
figs.20: C2DonationO route from FHD-104X. Terminal alkyne FC2D-101, iodoalkyne FC2D-102, deprotected FC2D-103. The drawn product carries an I cap.
figs.21: MeDonationO route from FHD-104X. Product FMeD-102 is drawn as Ge-CH2-I: the CH2 radical of FIG. 6 with an I cap.
figs.22: SiH3DonationO route. Starts from FHD-106 (FIG. 19), not FHD-104X. Mes esters replace free phenols (FSiHD-101), Si(OEt)3 is added at Ge (FSiHD-102), LiAlH4 ends at SiH3 with free phenols (FSiHD-103).
figs.23: GeH3DonationO route from FHD-104X. Ge-GeH2Ph (FGeHD-101), then acid and LiAlH4 give GeH3 with free phenols (FGeHD-102).
figs.24: SiMe3DonationO route. Same Mes protection as FIG. 22, then ClSiMe3 instead of ClSi(OEt)3; LiAlH4 only frees the phenols.
figs.25: GeMe3DonationO route from FHD-104X. One step to install GeMe3, one to remove TBDPS.
figs.26: AbstractNH route, NFA-1 to NFA-9. FIG. 18 with an aniline in place of the phenol: same bridgehead sequence, HBF4 salt before oxidation, Boc on N instead of TBS on O. Drawn reductant for NFA-5 is diisobutylaluminum hydride; [0150] names LiAlH4 for that step. The figure prints Pr_{3}NRuO_{4}; FIG. 18 prints Pr_{4} and [0142] has Pr4N.
figs.27: HDonationNH route from NHD-103X (FIG. 43). Ge-H (NHD-104), then deprotection (NHD-105). Legs drawn N(PMB)2, then NH2 after Pd(OH)2/H2; no O leg group appears.
figs.28: C2DonationNH route. TIPS-protected alkyne first; PMB comes off, then the silyl group, and iodination is last; FIG. 20 iodinates before removing its O protection. Legs drawn N(PMB)2, then NH2 after Pd(OH)2/H2; no O leg group appears.
figs.29: MeDonationNH route. Product NMeD-102 is drawn as Ge-CH2-I. Legs drawn N(PMB)2, then NH2 after Pd(OH)2/H2; no O leg group appears.
figs.30: SiH3DonationNH route. Si(OEt)3 on Ge, reduced to SiH3, then deprotection. Legs drawn N(PMB)2, then NH2 after Pd(OH)2/H2; no O leg group appears.
figs.31: GeH3DonationNH route. Ge-GeH2Ph, then GeH3, then deprotection. Legs drawn N(PMB)2, then NH2 after Pd(OH)2/H2; no O leg group appears.
figs.32: SiMe3DonationNH route. Legs drawn N(PMB)2, then NH2 after Pd(OH)2/H2; no O leg group appears.
figs.33: GeMe3DonationNH route. Legs drawn N(PMB)2, then NH2 after Pd(OH)2/H2; no O leg group appears.
figs.34: AbstractS route, SHA-1 to SHA-8. Phenyl rings are temporary: added to the cage, then oxidized to CO2H (SHA-3) and carried to the CH2-S legs through CH2OH and triflate. SHA-8 has free SH and an iodoalkyne cap. SHA-2 is reused in FIG. 50.
figs.35: HDonationS route. Same phenyl-to-CH2S leg sequence as FIG. 34, on the Ge cage RHD-101 (FIG. 42). The methyl on Ge survives until SHD-106X, where it becomes Ge-X, then Ge-H in SHD-107.
figs.36: C2DonationS route from SHD-106X (FIG. 35). Grignard installs the alkyne; iodination gives SC2D-102.
figs.37: MeDonationS route from SHD-105. Acetyl thiol protection is swapped for S-tBu before the Ge-X and Ge-CH2-I steps. The label SMeD-104 is "SMeDon-104" in the text [0161].
figs.38: SiH3DonationS route from SMeD-102X (FIG. 37). Figures 38-41 differ in the group put on Ge.
figs.39: GeH3DonationS route from SMeD-102X. Ge-GeH2Ph, then GeH3 with free SH.
figs.42: Common O-series intermediate FHD-104X. Starts from a printed "Commercially Available" cis-cyclohexane triacid. Ge enters at HD-3 and the cage closes at HD-4; RHD-101 is the branch point reused in FIG. 35 and FIG. 43, and HD-4 in FIG. 53.
figs.43: Common NH-series intermediate NHD-103X, from RHD-101 (FIG. 42) via an aniline coupling and PMB protection. Start point for FIG. 27-33.
figs.44: Photo-activation after mounting. 254 nm removes the I cap from the drawn tip, leaving the C2 radical of FIG. 3 plus an I radical.
figs.45: Photo-activation of the Barton ester cap at 365 nm. Byproducts drawn: CO2 and the pyrithiyl radical [0181]. The bound tip that remains is the same as in FIG. 44.
figs.46: Barton ester version of AbstractO. Branches from OFA-7 (FIG. 18). OFAB-1 adds the propynoic acid, OFAB-2 the ester, OFAB-3 frees the phenols under buffered conditions. Input to FIG. 45.
figs.47: Inverted mode [0087]. The workpiece, on the handle, moves between many fixed tips. Diagrammatic and not to scale [0183]. The four tips carry different end symbols (circle, triangle, two bare stubs) that the text does not key individually.
figs.48: Meta-tip [0091]. FIG. 47 turned over: the tips sit on the handle side and the workpiece stays on the lower surface. The positional means is not shown.
figs.49: Six interferometer beams for six degrees of freedom [0195]-[0196]. Beam pairs set the rotations: Z1-Z2 about x, Z2-Z3 about y, Y1-Y2 about z; the drawn pair spacings run roughly along y, x and x. Beam 4907 appears to pass behind mirror 4903, giving the two parallel lines under it.
figs.50: AdamRad-Br route from SHA-2 (FIG. 34). Iodination, Sonogashira coupling, TIPS removal, then formaldehyde gives AdBr-4, also called AdamRad-Br. New leg: phenylpropargyl alcohol [0199]. Br on the plain cage is the feedstock.
figs.51: Abstraction tip with propanol legs. Printed label is "PAO HAbst"; the text uses "PAO-AbstI" [0200] and "PAO-HAbstI" ([0068], Table 1). Step yields are printed. Used in the deposition experiments of [0203]-[0204].
figs.52: Methyl donation tool with CH2OH legs. Ge enters through Ge(CH2Cl)4 and the cage closes in one step (MG-110). Printed labels: MAO-GeRad-CH2I, "MAO-MeDonI". Step yields are printed. Used in the deposition experiments of [0203]-[0204].
figs.53: C2 donation tool with CH2CH2OH legs, from HD-4 (FIG. 42). A tert-butylphenyl group occupies Ge until BD-21. Printed product label is EAO-GeHAbstI; [0202] gives both EAO-C2DonI and EAO-GeHAbstI. Equivalents are printed, yields are not. Used in the deposition experiments of [0203]-[0204].

glossary.def: Use of positional control and mechanical force to drive site-specific chemical reactions; voltage bias is neither required nor excluded [0089].
Here a designed molecule, not the bare apex of a probe: active atoms that change bonding, plus support atoms that do not [0100].
Atomically precise tip made by bulk chemistry instead of by mechanosynthesis [0097].
Tip described as active site, body, legs, linkers and feedstock, so parts can be swapped [0092].
The atom or atoms that bind the group being moved [0121].
Rigid core holding active site and legs, adamantane-based here; also isolates the active site chemically [0124].
Leg attaches body to surface; linker is the end group that forms the surface bond: O, NH or S here [0125], [0127].
Atoms carried by a tip for adding to a workpiece; also atoms removed from one [0084].
Reaction removing an atom, typically hydrogen, from a workpiece onto the tip's radical site [0121], [0131].
Reaction transferring feedstock from tip to workpiece. Tip names give the feedstock: H, C2, Me, SiH3, GeH3, SiMe3, GeMe3 [0134].
O, NH or S gives the linker: AbstractO, HDonationNH, MeDonationS.
Atom with an unpaired electron, highly reactive. Drawn as a dot [0104].
Group that blocks a reactive active site during synthesis and mounting, removed afterwards, here by light [0123], [0179].
Thiohydroxamic ester cap that fragments under about 355-365 nm light into a carbon radical, CO2 and a pyrithiyl radical [0181].
C10H16 cage, the smallest unit cage of diamond [0072].
Adamantane with one cage carbon replaced by Ge, the donation tips' active site. Drawn with Ge at the apex.
Cage atom bonded to three other cage atoms; the legs and apex groups attach at these sites [0076].
Surface holding tips or feedstock, or supporting the workpiece [0094].
The object being built [0103].
Structure holding a tip or workpiece for the positional device [0085].
Device providing atomically precise positioning, e.g. a scanning probe microscope [0093].
Tip moves to a stationary workpiece, or workpiece moves to the tips [0080], [0087].
Tool carrying several tips [0091].
Ordered list of reactions that makes a workpiece [0077].
Making atomically precise tips from imprecise ones by mechanosynthesis, the step these tips aim to avoid [0009], [0106].
Scanning probe, atomic force and scanning tunneling microscope.
Quartz tuning-fork force sensor used in low-temperature atomic force microscopes, named in [0197].
Position error from small rotations when the measured point is offset from the working point [0194].
Temporary blocks on reactive groups during synthesis: TBS and TBDPS (silyl, on O), PMB and Boc (on N), Mes (mesitoate ester, on O), Ac (on S), S-tBu. Some are defined in the drawings.

OFA-1, FHD-105, NHD-103X and similar name intermediates and are used the same way in the text. X = Cl, Br, I. The document does not spell out the prefixes; in the drawings F and OFA mark phenol series, N and NFA aniline series, S and SHA thiol series.
